svg.title: The four mechanisms that stack before an accelerator is usable
svg.desc: Four layers, each resting on the one below. Layer 1, at the bottom, is the image: a Talos Image Factory schematic becomes the kernel and initramfs that BSS serves, so this layer loops back to the Talos assets of section 10 and is the only one OpenCHAMI serves. Layer 2 is drivers: Talos system extensions, baked into that boot image. Layer 3 is advertisement: a device plugin tells Kubernetes, for example, that a node has four nvidia.com/gpu. Layer 4, at the top, is scheduling: Ray resources, node selectors, and taints and tolerations decide which workload lands where. This proof of concept has no accelerators; what it establishes is the mechanisms, so that adding hardware is a configuration change rather than a research project.
svg.text: Read bottom to top: each layer needs the one below it. Blue is the one layer OpenCHAMI serves; grey is everything Kubernetes does on top.
Talos system extensions, baked into the boot image
Talos Image Factory schematic → the assets BSS serves
This proof of concept has no accelerators. It establishes the mechanisms, so adding hardware is a configuration change. Layer 1 loops back to §10.
